title: Value Scenarios
intro: Value scenarios are short stories about how a technology plays out for different people, including people who never use it, once it is widely used and has been around for years (Nathan, Klasnja & Friedman, 2007). In this lesson you will write a few scenarios, push them forward in time and across society, and trace the values they touch. Your scenarios carry over from step to step.

steps.title: Choose the technology
steps.task: Name the technology your scenarios are about. Be concrete: what does it do, and who uses it?
objectives: Names a specific technology and what it does

guide.label: {technology}
guide.where: The box at the top left of the panel below.

steps.title: Whose stories?
steps.task: List the people whose stories you will tell. Include at least one indirect stakeholder: someone affected by the technology who never uses it.
objectives: Includes at least one indirect stakeholder

guide.label: {stakeholders}
guide.where: Left of the scenario list. Add people yourself, or bring them in from your stakeholder map.

steps.title: Write a scenario
steps.task: Write a short story, a few sentences, about one stakeholder meeting the technology today. Make it specific: a person, a place, a moment. Then write another for a different stakeholder.
objectives: Tells a concrete story from one stakeholder’s point of view
Writes scenarios for at least two stakeholders

steps.title: Move it forward in time
steps.task: Jump ahead 5 or 20+ years in each scenario. What has changed for this person?
objectives: Describes how effects build up or change over the years

guide.label: Later
guide.where: In each scenario card: pick how far ahead, then write.

steps.title: Imagine everyone has it
steps.task: What happens when the technology is everywhere, not just in one home, school, or workplace?
objectives: Considers the effects of widespread use, not only of one user

steps.title: Trace systemic effects
steps.task: Follow the knock-on effects: how do institutions, social norms, or relationships change?
objectives: Identifies indirect effects on institutions, norms, or relationships

steps.title: Value implications
steps.task: Tag each scenario with the values it touches, and mark each one as a harm or a benefit.
objectives: Names the values at stake in each scenario
Marks whether each value is harmed or supported

guide.label: {values}
guide.where: At the bottom of each scenario card. Pick {harm} or {benefit}, type, press Enter.

steps.title: Compare scenarios
steps.task: Put your scenarios side by side. Where does one stakeholder’s benefit come at another’s cost? Record the tensions.
objectives: Identifies at least one tension between scenarios
